From 36f46b0e36892eba08978eef7502ff3c94ddba77 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Thorsten Blum <thorsten.blum@linux.dev>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 00:00:09 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] crash_dump: don't log dm-crypt key bytes in
 read_key_from_user_keying

When debug logging is enabled, read_key_from_user_keying() logs the first
8 bytes of the key payload and partially exposes the dm-crypt key.  Stop
logging any key bytes.

Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20260227230008.858641-2-thorsten.blum@linux.dev
Fixes: 479e58549b0f ("crash_dump: store dm crypt keys in kdump reserved memory")
Signed-off-by: Thorsten Blum <thorsten.blum@linux.dev>
Cc: Baoquan He <bhe@redhat.com>
Cc: Coiby Xu <coxu@redhat.com>
Cc: Dave Young <dyoung@redhat.com>
Cc: Vivek Goyal <vgoyal@redhat.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/kernel/crash_dump_dm_crypt.c b/kernel/crash_dump_dm_crypt.c
index 1f4067fbdb94..a20d4097744a 100644
--- a/kernel/crash_dump_dm_crypt.c
+++ b/kernel/crash_dump_dm_crypt.c
@@ -168,8 +168,8 @@ static int read_key_from_user_keying(struct dm_crypt_key *dm_key)
 
 	memcpy(dm_key->data, ukp->data, ukp->datalen);
 	dm_key->key_size = ukp->datalen;
-	kexec_dprintk("Get dm crypt key (size=%u) %s: %8ph\n", dm_key->key_size,
-		      dm_key->key_desc, dm_key->data);
+	kexec_dprintk("Get dm crypt key (size=%u) %s\n", dm_key->key_size,
+		      dm_key->key_desc);
 
 out:
 	up_read(&key->sem);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `kernel/crash_dump_dm_crypt.c`
- **Function**: `read_key_from_user_keying()`
- **Modification**: Removed the hex dump (`%8ph`) of the first 8 bytes of the DM crypt key from the `kexec_dprintk` debug message.  
  - **Before**: Logged key size, key description, and the first 8 key bytes.  
  - **After**: Logs only key size and key description, omitting any key payload data.

### Relationships
- **Single file change**: All modifications are isolated to one function in one file.
- **Security fix**: The change prevents inadvertent exposure of cryptographic key material in kernel debug logs, addressing a potential information leak vulnerability. No other functional logic or control flow was altered.

This patch ensures that when debug logging is enabled, the DM crypt key bytes are not printed, thereby enhancing security.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
kexec_dprintk("Get dm crypt key (size=%u) %s: %8ph\n", dm_key->key_size,
              dm_key->key_desc, dm_key->data);
```
Reason:
This debug log uses the `%8ph` format specifier to print the first 8 bytes of `dm_key->data`, which contains the raw dm-crypt key material. When `kexec_dprintk` is enabled (e.g., via dynamic debug or kernel configuration), these key bytes are exposed in the kernel log, constituting a cryptographic information leak. The vulnerability allows anyone with access to the kernel log to obtain partial key data.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
kexec_dprintk("Get dm crypt key (size=%u) %s\n", dm_key->key_size,
              dm_key->key_desc);
```
Reason:
The fix removes the `%8ph` format specifier and its argument `dm_key->data` from the debug print. The revised log line only prints the key size and description, avoiding any exposure of the key payload itself. This ensures that even with debug logging enabled, no cryptographic material is inadvertently leaked.
